title: Do You Need Both Gong and a Real-Time Assistant?
summary: Gong analyses calls after they end. A real-time assistant helps during them. When pairing both makes sense, and how the Caretta + Gong integration works.
body_markdown:
Yes, if you can afford both: Gong and a real-time assistant solve different problems, and pairing them covers the full life of a call. Gong tells you what happened across every conversation; a real-time assistant changes what happens inside the one going on right now. The Caretta + Gong integration makes the pair work as one system.


## 01


What Gong does well


Gong records, transcribes, and analyses calls at scale. Managers see talk ratios, topic trends, competitor mentions, and deal risk across hundreds of conversations a month. Coaching gets grounded in real recordings instead of hearsay, and forecast reviews get evidence behind them. Teams that run Gong properly know their pipeline in a way teams without it simply do not.


Its structural limit is timing: everything Gong tells you arrives after the call ends. It can show you, precisely, that a rep went quiet when the buyer asked about SOC 2. That insight improves next week's calls. It did nothing for the deal on the line that day. We compared the two categories in depth in[conversation intelligence vs real-time call guidance](https://www.caretta.so/blog/conversation-intelligence-vs-real-time) ; the short version is that they answer different questions, for different people, at different moments.


## 02


What a real-time assistant adds


A real-time assistant works during the call, for the rep. When the hard question lands, it surfaces the answer: the security posture, the pricing logic, the case study, the way your best rep handles exactly this objection. The rep responds in the moment instead of promising to "get back to you," and the deal keeps its momentum.


Real-time tools have honest limits of their own. Help that arrives ten seconds late is noise, and help that arrives too often trains reps to ignore it. A good assistant is quiet on easy calls and decisive on hard ones, and any evaluation should test exactly that: bring your three ugliest recurring objections to the demo and watch the timing.


That is the job Caretta was built for. It learns from your docs, CRM, past calls, and top performers, and it helps before, during, and after every meeting. It does not try to be an analytics platform, for the same reason Gong does not try to whisper answers mid-call: they are different jobs, and each is hard to do well.


## 03


How does the Caretta + Gong integration work?


The pairing is not two tools running side by side; it is one feeding the other. Caretta connects to your Gong call history and learns from it.


That history is one of the most valuable knowledge assets a sales team owns. Years of recorded conversations hold every objection your market raises and every answer that worked. Inside Gong, that knowledge is searchable after the fact. Piped into Caretta, it becomes usable live: when a buyer raises an objection, the guidance drawing on hundreds of past calls arrives while the rep can still act on it.


In practice:


1. **Connect Gong** from Caretta's[integrations](https://www.caretta.so/integrations) page. Caretta ingests call history into its organisational memory alongside your docs and CRM.
2. **Caretta learns the patterns** : which questions come up, how the best reps answer them, what language wins in your market.
3. **On live calls** , that learning surfaces as real-time help, grounded in your own conversations rather than generic sales advice.
4. **Gong keeps doing its job.** Calls still land in Gong, dashboards still update, coaching workflows stay intact.


The connection is read-only. Caretta learns from Gong's history and writes nothing back to it, so there is no risk to the analytics, scorecards, or coaching workflows your managers depend on. If the pairing ever stops earning its keep, disconnecting it costs nothing.


## 04


Where should the line sit between Gong and Caretta?


Question Answer lives in


How is the team performing this quarter? Gong


Is this forecast real? Gong


What should I say to this objection, right now? Caretta


What does our security posture actually cover? Caretta


Which reps need coaching, on what? Gong


Can my new rep survive a technical call alone? Caretta


The pattern: retrospective and aggregate questions belong to Gong; live and individual ones belong to Caretta. Managers and RevOps live in the first set. Reps mid-call live in the second.


Respecting that line matters when you evaluate either tool. Gong has added assistant-style features, and real-time tools advertise analytics. Judge each on its core job, and treat the rest as a bonus. Buying one tool to do both jobs usually gets you one job done well and one done badly; the honest comparison for Gong's own live-assist offering is in[Kaia vs Gong](https://www.caretta.so/blog/kaia-vs-gong) .


## 05


When one tool is enough


Both is not always the right answer. If your team is small and deals die inside the calls themselves, real-time guidance is the higher-order bit and Gong can wait. If your calls are fine but leadership is blind to the pipeline, conversation intelligence is the priority. The pairing earns its cost when a team has both problems at once: enough reps that visibility matters, and enough hard calls that in-the-moment help changes outcomes.


If you already pay for Gong, the integration is the cheapest upgrade available: the call library you have spent years building starts working during calls, not just after them.
